name: Curtis Sliwa
role: Founder of the Guardian Angels; Republican nominee for New York City mayor (2021, 2025)
summary: Sliwa is a law-and-order Republican who built his public profile on citizen street patrols and radio commentary. His platform centres on more police, subway safety, cutting property taxes, ending congestion pricing and rolling back the City of Yes zoning plan. He has an independent streak, including a self-described love/hate relationship with Trump, and is known for animal welfare causes such as no-kill shelters.

sources.usedFor: His 2025 platform in his campaign's words: stronger city EITC, opposition to the City of Yes and Charter ballot questions, 7,000 more police, keeping Rikers open, ending the charter cap; a candidate's platform is words, not record

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Opposes defund-the-police efforts and proposes adding thousands of officers.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Supports ending the killing of unwanted dogs and cats in city shelters (no-kill model); runs a cat rescue.

decide-locally.rationale: His 2025 platform opposes charter changes that would 'concentrate the power of development in the hands of whomever will be the Mayor forever' and promises to work with every council member and precinct on local needs.

direct-votes.rationale: Promised to put sanctuary city laws and Rikers closure to voters via a Charter Revision Commission, but opposed all six ballot proposals in 2025; not a general stance.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: His 2025 platform ('Make Work Pay') pledges to 'champion a higher New York City EITC match in the state budget with city co-funding to unlock larger refunds' because the credit 'is proven to reward work and support families'.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: In the 2025 debate he said he would increase prostitution enforcement, treat women as victims, and prosecute pimps, madams and landlords; he did not address legalization for consenting adults directly.

local-veto-new-housing.rationale: Campaigned against City of Yes and Charter ballot questions 2, 3 and 4 as taking 'away your vote' on land use from the City Council and 'the voice' of residents and 'giving developers the floodgates'; he wants neighbourhoods to keep control of zoning.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wikipedia reports support for separation of church and state; in 2021 he said parochial schools should provide secular education to qualify for state funding.

notes:
Most platform specifics (bail, taxes, homelessness, rent, congestion pricing, charter schools, sanctuary city, Trump) match no statement in the list, so they are not recorded as answers. Debate coverage rather than transcripts was used (see notFound). Social-issue answers rest on Wikipedia and are low confidence.

Later pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-14): brought to rules 7. The two Wikipedia/OnTheIssues-only social answers (same-sex-marriage, abortion-legal) are nulled after searching MediaSum (75 clips: policing, Guardian Angels, none on these topics) and the 2021 and 2025 campaign interviews (WNYC, Queens Eagle, amNY, ABC7, CBS): none states a position. The platform items (bail, taxes, congestion pricing, charter schools, sanctuary city) still match no bank statement. Deeper push (same day): read the 2025 campaign platform pages (sliwafornyc.com: 100 Day Plan, safety, Rikers, housing, schools, commute, protecting neighborhoods; ~14,000 words) and the 2021 campaign site (Wayback). They are candidate platform, i.e. words. New answers: in-work-tax-credits +2, local-veto-new-housing +1, decide-locally +1. Most platform items match no bank wording: 7,000 more NYPD officers and 'proactive and intrusive' policing, keeping Rikers open, ending the charter school cap (not vouchers), no tax on tips, congestion-pricing rebate, property-tax relief, migrant spending, bail reform rollback. Debate transcripts: read the debate coverage already cited (s3, s5).
